title: Protecting the root user with MFA

kcs.statement: Multi-factor authentication requires a second factor in addition to the password, such as a code from a virtual authenticator app, a FIDO2 passkey or security key, or a hardware TOTP token.
To protect the root user: enable MFA, set a strong password, do not create root access keys (delete any that exist), and sign in as root only for root-only tasks.
MFA should be enabled for every human identity with console access, not only the root user, because it stops a stolen password alone from granting access.
